newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Italian president says supports Macedonia EU entry.
newsitem.headline: Italian president says supports Macedonia EU entry.

text.p: Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said on Wednesday he supported Macedonia's bid to become a full member of the European Union and NATO.
After talks with Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov in the Macedonian capital Skopje, Scalfaro told reporters: "Italy supports Macedonian integration in the EU and NATO...and its path of democracy."

He said Macedonia represented stability in the "turbulent Balkan region" and Italy would actively support cooperation within the framework of the NATO partnership for peace initiative in which both countries participate.

In an address to the Skopje parliament Scalfaro said bilateral ties could lead to further political, economic and cultural development which would be in the interest of both countries and in the interest of peace in the region.
Macedonia proclaimed its independence in 1991 and was the only republic of the former Yugoslavia to secede peacefully.
It was badly hit by United Nations sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia in 1992 as sixty percent of its industrial production was closely linked with neighbouring Serbia and Montenegro.
Gligorov emphasised the importance of Italy which is Macedonia's second biggest foreign trade partner.
"Italy has a significant role in the Balkan peace process. Being well aware of the Italian position in the EU NATO and the Security Council, Macedonia asks for Italian support," he said.
Gligorov said both countries were interested in constructing an East-West trade corridor to connect Europe to Asia, across the Adriatic sea and through the Balkans.
Scalfaro signed an agreement protecting Italian investment in Macedonia and covering cooperation between the countries' foreign ministries.
